goal_text: I want to learn about AI

nodes.title: What do we actually mean by "AI"?
nodes.one_liner: Defines AI plainly; clears up hype and sci-fi myths.

nodes.title: How does a machine "learn"?
nodes.one_liner: The core idea behind machine learning, no math.

nodes.title: The main flavors of AI
nodes.one_liner: Key types: prediction, vision, language, generation.

nodes.title: How do tools like ChatGPT work?
nodes.one_liner: What large language models do and why they feel smart.

nodes.title: Where AI gets things wrong
nodes.one_liner: Bias, hallucinations, and other real limitations.

nodes.title: What AI can and can't do today
nodes.one_liner: Honest picture of current strengths and hard limits.

nodes.title: Why AI matters right now
nodes.one_liner: Real-world impact on jobs, society, daily life.

outline.rationale: The user is a total beginner wanting breadth and a solid working mental model, explicitly non-technical and not focused on building or careers. I start with definition (clearing hype), then the foundational concept of learning, then a survey of AI types so they have a map. Because generative AI/chatbots are the dominant public face of AI and likely their real curiosity, a dedicated node on LLMs is warranted. I split limitations into two complementary angles—failure modes (bias/hallucination) and overall capability boundaries—because for a beginner, distinguishing "how it fails" from "what it fundamentally can't do" builds calibrated intuition. I close with societal relevance since they asked why it matters now. I excluded history, math, coding, tooling, and career paths per the confirmed understanding. Nodes are largely non-overlapping: definition vs. mechanism vs. taxonomy vs. one deep example vs. failures vs. capability frontier vs. impact.
